concept.name: Maximal extractable value
concept.definition: Maximal extractable value (MEV) is the maximum value that can be extracted from block production — beyond the standard block reward and gas fees — by including, excluding, or reordering transactions within a block.
concept.intuition: Whoever decides the order of transactions in a block holds a printing press: they can see the future of the block and sell positions in it.
concept.mechanics: Validators (formerly miners, hence the older term 'miner extractable value') control inclusion and ordering; in practice independent 'searchers' find opportunities — DEX arbitrage, liquidations, sandwich attacks — and capture them via gas bidding or sealed bundles (Flashbots/MEV-Boost), sharing most proceeds with validators through builder auctions (proposer-builder separation).
concept.failure_modes: Unchecked MEV degrades user execution (sandwiches), congests the network via gas auctions, and — when MEV in a block exceeds the block reward — creates incentives for time-bandit reorgs that threaten consensus stability; private order flow and builder concentration centralize the network.
concept.misconceptions: MEV is not inherently theft or purely bad — arbitrage and liquidations keep prices consistent and lending protocols solvent. Nor is it eliminable by protocol upgrades alone; it is an intrinsic property of ordering power, only redistributable or mitigated.
concept.example: A searcher spots ETH/DAI priced differently on Uniswap vs Sushiswap and turns 1,000 ETH into 1,045 ETH in one atomic transaction, paying most of the 45 ETH profit to the validator as a bribe for guaranteed inclusion.

citations.source: Ethereum.org developer docs - Maximal extractable value (MEV)
